page: Amazon Web Services m9gd.48xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor and custom ARMv9-based AWS Graviton Neoverse-V3 processors. It features 192 dedicated physical cores running at 2.8 GHz with a 1.0 thread-per-core ratio, eliminating simultaneous multithreading overhead. The system is equipped with 768.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB per core. Local storage is bundled as 11,400 GB of NVMe SSD instance store volumes, and the instance delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 100 Gbps.

Benchmark data highlights top-tier multi-core CPU and memory performance. The instance achieves a top-tier stress-ng multi-core score of 382,376.39 and a PassMark CPU score of 107,019.88. Memory bandwidth is exceptionally high, with cached read-only small block speeds reaching 27,785.94 GB/sec and uncached large block write speeds at 327.45 GB/sec. Additionally, the instance demonstrates top-tier efficiency in data decompression, static web serving throughput at 358.31 GB/sec, and Redis SET operations processing 506.95 million operations per second.

While multi-core and database operations rank in the top tier, single-core performance is moderate, with a stress-ng single-core score of 2,009.1. Furthermore, LLM inference on small 135M models shows weak prompt processing and poor text generation speeds, though prompt processing for medium 7B models remains in the top tier. Given the high resource density of 192 dedicated ARM64 cores, massive local NVMe storage, and high memory bandwidth, this instance is highly cost-efficient for scale-out workloads. It is best suited for high-throughput database operations, large-scale web serving, multi-threaded data compression, and memory-intensive general-purpose applications.
